payload.task_text:
I need a comprehensive coupon performance report for our marketing team. Please pull our coupon data from the store and analyze the effectiveness of each coupon code.

Create an Excel file called Coupon_Performance.xlsx with a sheet called Coupon Analysis that has columns for Coupon_Code, Discount_Type, Discount_Amount, Times_Used, Usage_Limit (the per-coupon total usage limit — use N/A if the coupon has no total usage limit set), and Usage_Rate_Pct which is calculated as Times_Used divided by Usage_Limit multiplied by one hundred rounded to two decimal places — use N/A if there is no usage limit. Sort by Times_Used in descending order. Add a second sheet called Summary with Metric and Value columns showing the following rows: Total_Coupons, Most_Used_Coupon with the code that has the highest usage count, Highest_Discount with the code that has the largest discount amount value, and Total_Coupon_Uses as the sum of all usage counts across all coupons.

After the Excel, create a PowerPoint presentation called Coupon_Analysis_Presentation.pptx. Include a title slide titled Coupon Performance Analysis, one slide for each coupon showing the code, discount type, and usage count, and a final summary slide with the overall statistics.

Create a Notion page titled Coupon Strategy Overview 2026 with key findings from the coupon analysis including which coupons are performing best and recommendations. The page content should reference at least one of the top-performing coupon codes (for example HOLIDAY30, SAVE20, or FLASH50) and include explicit performance analysis and actionable recommendations written into the page body (not just the title).

Send an email to marketing@company.com with subject Coupon Campaign Performance Report Q1 2026 containing a brief summary of the coupon performance results.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, complete it directly in the main agent; dispatch no sub-agent. The coupon catalog is compact, and every deliverable consumes one canonical small calculation table, so delegation would add a handoff without shortening a real dependency.

Resolve the task-visible workspace dynamically. Retrieve the complete coupon catalog read-only with `woo_coupons_list`, using `perPage=100` and increasing `page` until a short or empty terminal page; retain coupon code, discount type, numeric amount, `usage_count`, and the total `usage_limit`, preserving an absent or zero total limit as no limit. Freeze one coupon-code-keyed table before writing anything. Compute `Usage_Rate_Pct = Times_Used / Usage_Limit * 100` only for a positive total limit, rounded to two decimals and stored as a literal number; otherwise store the literal text `N/A`. Explicitly read back every coupon row, especially limited coupons, so a numeric rate is never omitted. Derive the four Summary values from this canonical frozen table with deterministic tie handling based on source order.

The main agent is the sole writer of `Coupon_Performance.xlsx`, `Coupon_Analysis_Presentation.pptx`, and the exact-title knowledge-base page. Before any external create, exhaust the supported Notion search pages for exact title `Coupon Strategy Overview 2026`: reuse one exact match, create exactly once only on zero matches, and block page writes on multiple exact matches or an ambiguous create failure. In parallel, exhaust Sent-mail pages for the task's exact recipient and subject; retain one exact match and record send-needed only when none exists. Create each local artifact once and keep every identifier/path for all subsequent operations. After the coupon table is frozen, interleave the independent workbook, presentation, and page branches with native parallel tool calls whenever their next calls are simultaneously ready; do not create a verification wave. The presentation must contain exactly the task-requested title slide, one complete coupon slide per frozen coupon, and the final summary slide. The page body—not only its title—must name verified top-performing coupon codes, explain their observed performance, and give actionable recommendations. Read back both workbook sheets, the presentation slide inventory/content, and the retained page ID/body. Only when the exact Sent search recorded no match, send the required email at most once from the verified summary; never retry an ambiguous send, and read back the retained or newly sent message ID. Complete any remaining original requirement and call `claim_done` if available.

You are building two local office artifacts (an Excel workbook and a PowerPoint deck) from pre-analyzed WooCommerce coupon data. All data is provided below — do NOT query WooCommerce or search for anything; just build the files.

Save both files in this workspace directory: /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_Qwen3.8-Max/SingleUserTurn-wc-coupon-performance-notion-ppt/workspace

DELIVERABLE 1: Excel workbook named exactly "Coupon_Performance.xlsx"

Sheet 1 must be named exactly "Coupon Analysis". Columns (header row): Coupon_Code, Discount_Type, Discount_Amount, Times_Used, Usage_Limit, Usage_Rate_Pct.
Rows, in this exact order (already sorted by Times_Used descending):

| Coupon_Code | Discount_Type | Discount_Amount | Times_Used | Usage_Limit | Usage_Rate_Pct |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| HOLIDAY30 | percent | 30 | 50 | 100 | 50 |
| VIP20 | percent | 20 | 41 | N/A | N/A |
| SAVE20 | fixed_cart | 20 | 39 | 50 | 78 |
| WELCOME10 | percent | 10 | 23 | 100 | 23 |
| BULK10 | percent | 10 | 17 | N/A | N/A |
| ELECTRONICS15 | percent | 15 | 16 | N/A | N/A |
| FREESHIP | fixed_cart | 0 | 10 | N/A | N/A |
| SUMMER25 | percent | 25 | 9 | 200 | 4.5 |
| FLASH50 | fixed_cart | 50 | 2 | 30 | 6.67 |
| NEWUSER5 | fixed_cart | 5 | 2 | N/A | N/A |

Rules:
- Usage_Limit is the string "N/A" where the coupon had no total usage limit; otherwise the numeric limit.
- Usage_Rate_Pct = Times_Used / Usage_Limit * 100 rounded to two decimals; write numeric values (50.0 -> 50, 78.0 -> 78, 23.0 -> 23, 4.5, 6.67) and apply a "0.00" number format to those numeric cells so they display as 50.00, 78.00, 23.00, 4.50, 6.67. Where Usage_Limit is N/A, Usage_Rate_Pct must be the string "N/A".
- Discount_Amount: write as numbers (30, 20, 20, 10, 10, 15, 0, 25, 50, 5).

Sheet 2 must be named exactly "Summary" with header row "Metric", "Value" and these rows in this order:
- Total_Coupons | 10
- Most_Used_Coupon | HOLIDAY30
- Highest_Discount | FLASH50
- Total_Coupon_Uses | 209

Make headers bold. If the workbook's default first sheet already exists, you may write to it and rename it to "Coupon Analysis" rather than creating a duplicate.

DELIVERABLE 2: PowerPoint deck named exactly "Coupon_Analysis_Presentation.pptx" (save the presentation file with that name in the workspace directory above).

Structure:
1. Title slide with title "Coupon Performance Analysis" (subtitle like "Q1 2026 Marketing Report" is fine).
2. One slide for EACH of the 10 coupons (10 slides) in the sorted order above. Each slide must clearly show: the coupon code (use it as slide title), the discount type, and the usage count. E.g. slide titled "HOLIDAY30" with bullets: "Code: HOLIDAY30", "Discount Type: percent (30%)", "Times Used: 50". Use the coupon's actual amount for the percent/dollar description (percent coupons: "percent (X%)"; fixed_cart coupons: "fixed_cart ($X)"). You may also include the usage-limit row ("Usage Limit: 100" or "Usage Limit: N/A (unlimited)") and usage rate where applicable — optional but nice. FREESHIP is fixed_cart $0 offering free shipping.
3. Final summary slide titled "Summary" (or "Overall Summary") containing these statistics:
   - Total Coupons: 10
   - Total Coupon Uses: 209
   - Most Used Coupon: HOLIDAY30 (50 uses)
   - Highest Discount: FLASH50 ($50 off)

Use whatever create/slide/text tools work; the key acceptance criteria are the exact file names in the workspace directory, sheet names, columns, sorted rows, N/A handling, and the slide structure above.

When done, verify by reading back the Excel data (both sheets) and confirming the file exists, then report: exact file paths, sheet names, row counts, and a summary of the slide titles you created.
Build Excel and PPTX files

You need to perform two external actions based on a completed WooCommerce coupon performance analysis. All data is provided below — do NOT query WooCommerce; just create the Notion page and send the email.

ANALYSIS RESULTS (10 coupons, Q1 2026):
Sorted by usage count:
1. HOLIDAY30 — percent, 30% off, 50 uses, limit 100 → 50.00% usage rate (top performer by volume)
2. VIP20 — percent, 20% off, 41 uses, no total limit
3. SAVE20 — fixed_cart $20 off, 39 uses, limit 50 → 78.00% usage rate (highest utilization, nearly exhausted)
4. WELCOME10 — percent, 10% off, 23 uses, limit 100 → 23.00% usage rate
5. BULK10 — percent, 10% off, 17 uses, no limit
6. ELECTRONICS15 — percent, 15% off, 16 uses, no limit
7. FREESHIP — fixed_cart, free shipping, 10 uses, no limit
8. SUMMER25 — percent, 25% off, 9 uses, limit 200 → 4.50% usage rate (underperforming)
9. FLASH50 — fixed_cart $50 off, 2 uses, limit 30 → 6.67% usage rate (largest discount value but underperforming)
10. NEWUSER5 — fixed_cart $5 off, 2 uses, no limit
Totals: 10 coupons, 209 total uses. Most used: HOLIDAY30. Largest discount amount: FLASH50.

TASK 1 — Create a Notion page titled exactly "Coupon Strategy Overview 2026".
Create it at the workspace level (parent: workspace). The page BODY must contain substantive content (not just the title): key findings from the analysis, performance analysis, and actionable recommendations. It must explicitly reference at least one top-performing code among HOLIDAY30, SAVE20, FLASH50 in the body text.

Use this content (you may lightly adjust formatting into Notion blocks — headings, bulleted lists):

Heading: Key Findings
- HOLIDAY30 is the top-performing coupon with 50 uses (50.00% of its 100-use limit consumed).
- SAVE20 has the highest utilization rate at 78.00% (39 of 50 allowed uses) and is close to being exhausted.
- VIP20 (41 uses) and WELCOME10 (23 uses) show strong ongoing demand for percentage-based loyalty and acquisition discounts.
- FLASH50 offers the largest discount value ($50 fixed cart discount) but has been used only 2 times (6.67% of its 30-use limit), making it the biggest underperformer.
- SUMMER25 is also underperforming at 4.50% usage rate (9 of 200 uses).
- Across all 10 coupons there were 209 total coupon uses this period.

Heading: Recommendations
- Extend or raise the usage limit of SAVE20 before it sells out; it converts at the highest rate (78%).
- Replicate the HOLIDAY30 seasonal percentage-discount model for upcoming campaigns, and consider increasing its limit since it is already at 50% redemption with months of validity left.
- Rework FLASH50: test a lower minimum order value or stronger promotion channels, since the $50 fixed discount is barely being redeemed (6.67%).
- Keep percentage-based coupons (VIP20, WELCOME10) as the core strategy — percent coupons account for the majority of redemptions.
- Review or retire low performers such as SUMMER25 and NEWUSER5, or bundle them with higher-traffic campaigns.

TASK 2 — Send an email to: marketing@company.com
Subject exactly: Coupon Campaign Performance Report Q1 2026
Body — a brief summary of the coupon performance results. Include these specifics: 10 active coupons analyzed, 209 total uses; HOLIDAY30 leads with 50 uses; SAVE20 nearly exhausted at 78% utilization (39/50); FLASH50 ($50 fixed discount) underperforming at 6.67%; mention that full analysis is available in Coupon_Performance.xlsx, Coupon_Analysis_Presentation.pptx, and the Notion page "Coupon Strategy Overview 2026". Plain text body is fine (HTML optional).

When done, report: the Notion page ID/URL and the email confirmation result.
